title: what the market actually *supports*
dek: A privacy-safe, externally researched decision brief for The Angle Map and the company-intelligence install: customer triggers, paid alternatives, proof boundaries, one controlled message test, and the exact evidence still missing.
lens: customer truth · category economics · message-market fit

sections.heading: the commercial verdict
sections.body:
TEST The Angle Map. The adjacent category is paid and the buyer job is sharper: make one defensible, production-usable argument before a launch, retail, claims, creator, or media window closes. The exact $750 offer remains untested.

NARROW the company-intelligence install to one paid, shadow-mode responsibility. Public evidence supports narrow work units, not a broad premium AI employee. The custom layer must beat the buyer's native platform on checked business-specific judgment.

rows.claim: The real Angle Map job is a production decision, not more ideas
rows.evidence: Reformulations, retail moves, consumer tests, claims review, creator programs, and printer deadlines repeatedly force one argument to connect product truth, permitted proof, channel logic, and creative execution.
FTC guidance covers express and implied claims across packaging, digital content, influencers, agencies, and intermediaries; proof mapping cannot be deferred to a disclaimer.

rows.claim: The broad AI employee is not a problem-qualified segment
rows.evidence: Government and industry evidence supports uneven AI adoption and narrow operational use. Public deployment proof is strongest for calls, intake, booking, routine support, and reports—not a premium company-intelligence employee.

rows.claim: Generic agent capability is being compressed
rows.evidence: Public agent platforms sell increasingly capable workflows for tens to hundreds of dollars per month, forcing a custom install to prove a workflow-specific judgment advantage.

sections.heading: what this *still doesn't prove*
sections.body: The research verifies category existence, public prices, regulatory constraints, repeat trigger patterns, platform compression, and narrow AI work-unit deployments. It does not verify internal prospect pain, exact-offer willingness to pay, collected revenue, campaign lift, or repeatable economics. All five notes remain discovery hypotheses and no external message has been sent.
